card.name: Tsifteteli
card.era: Ottoman-era origin; entered the Greek mainland after the 1922 population exchange
card.tagline: The Greek 'belly dance' in 4/4, of Anatolian origin.
card.profile: A rhythm and dance of Anatolia and the Balkans, the Greek counterpart of Turkish ciftetelli (Turkish 'double-stringed,' from a violin technique). In Greece it functions as the Greek 'belly dance': a solo improvisational form with hip undulations, shoulder shimmies and sinuous arm movements, typically in 4/4 (also cited as 2/4). Performed informally at weddings, glentia and festivals, mostly initiated by women; also professionally in tavernas and bouzouki clubs. Accompanied by violin, bouzouki and percussion; common in rebetiko/laiko (English Wikipedia; Folkdance Footnotes).
card.insight: Greek tsifteteli (one 'l') and Turkish ciftetelli (double 'l') share Ottoman roots but are documented as separate Wikipedia/Wikidata entities; Greeks often use 'tsifteteli' as a synonym for oriental dance generally.
